business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (2020 revision); Measures for the Management of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective Nov 1, 2024); Regulations on the Administration of Market Entities Registration (2022); Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Insurance Assessment Institutions (CBIRC, now under NFRA); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act as applicable to shareholder due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (recent company registration certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Contracting State: (1) notarize the certificate at a Taiwan district court notary; (2) legalize it through the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (3) complete the cross-strait notarized document verification procedure via the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait (ARATS). Do not apply a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / current company registration history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization / cross-strait authentication path using Taiwan court notary, Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, and SEF/ARATS document verification; no Hague Apostille permitted for Taiwan-origin instruments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for WFOE formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization / cross-strait authentication path: notarize corporate signatures before a Taiwan district court notary, have the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs certify the notary's seal, then authenticate the instrument through SEF/ARATS; a Hague Apostille obtained in any other member state cannot substitute.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization / cross-strait authentication path: notarize the consolidated updated articles, certify at Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and verify the notarized copy through SEF/ARATS before submission to Chinese SAMR and the licensing authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Taiwanese commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank acting for the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization / cross-strait authentication path: notarize the bank officer's signature, have the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalize the bank's corporate seal, then transmit the notarized letter through SEF/ARATS verification; do not chain this with a Hague Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, shareholder, director, supervisor, and authorized signatory against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, China's Ministry of Commerce prohibited and restricted sanctions lists, China's Financial Action Task Force-style AML lists, Taiwan's AML/CFT designated person list, EU restrictive measures, and reputable adverse media and PEP databases. Any PEP, sanctioned individual, or high-risk jurisdiction link requires written enhanced due diligence approval from the compliance committee before incorporation. Screening must be repeated at signing, pre-filing, and license application dates, with all results and audit trails retained for 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System - Enterprise Name Self-Declaration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters. The Taiwan investor's corporate name must be transliterated into standard pinyin where used as the distinctive element. The name must follow China's four-tier enterprise naming sequence: administrative division, distinctive name, industry or organization character (marine insurance survey / insurance assessment), and company type (limited liability company). English-only names are not accepted in the registry except as a registered foreign name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative reconsideration to the same SAMR authority within 60 days of the rejection notice, or six months for administrative litigation. The appeal must identify the refused name, quote the rejection code, rebut the claim of confusion or sensitivity, and provide supporting business-licensing proof. If the rejection is based on a pending insurance-assessment license, the applicant may re-file after NFRA pre-approval. The 30-day name reservation may be extended once by re-applying in the online portal before expiry, unless the registered business scope has changed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office, virtual mailbox, or bare agent address is not permissible for this WFOE. Local SAMR, tax bureaus, and banks reject a non-physical address for a licensed marine insurance surveying company. The company must hold a real leased or owned office in the municipal district of registration, documented by a valid lease agreement, landlord property-ownership proof, rent receipts, and utility records. A virtual address will cause bank account refusal, invoice-limit restrictions, and may block the NFRA insurance assessment license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk: Medium-High (estimated 35-45% likelihood in the first full year) due to the licensed financial-services-adjacent business. Unannounced on-site inspectors from municipal SAMR, tax authorities, or the local financial regulatory bureau will check: business license display; actual office sign; registered address match; staff presence; survey equipment and instruments; retained vessel and cargo claim files; insurance assessment qualification certificates; statutory records and accounting books; original leases; utility bills; and compliance and AML notices. The company should maintain a dedicated archive room and 10-year retention policy.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 1, 2, 129, 131, 145, 156, 161-1, 172, 192, 203 and 208; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12; Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Foreign Nationals; Insurance Law, Articles 163 and related qualification provisions; Regulations Governing Insurance Surveyors; Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) through the Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Service; Investment Commission, MOEA for Foreign Investment Approval; Insurance Bureau, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) for the marine insurance surveying license.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form together with Articles of Incorporation, First Board Meeting Minutes, CPA Capital Verification Report, and Foreign Investment Approval Letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a company limited by shares under the Taiwan Company Act following the 2018 amendment. No blocked escrow account is required. The subscribed capital must be fully paid into a corporate bank account in Taiwan before registration and verified by a Certified Public Accountant capital verification report. If capital is remitted from outside the Taiwan jurisdiction, the remittance must be reported through a designated foreign exchange bank and evidenced by a Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate, retained for regulatory inspection.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a company limited by shares to be incorporated under the Company Act of the Taiwan jurisdiction. RESOLVED, that the incorporator and the initial subscribers, acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of an organizational meeting, do hereby approve the following actions: 1. Subscription of Share Capital. Each subscriber shall acquire, and the Company shall issue to each subscriber, the number of ordinary shares set forth in the Subscription Schedule, with a par value of NT$10 per share, for an aggregate paid-in capital of NT$[●]. The Chairperson and the General Manager are jointly and severally authorized to collect the subscription proceeds in cash or bank transfer, to deposit the proceeds into a corporate bank account held in the name of the Company, and to procure a certified public accountant capital verification report in accordance with Article 145 of the Company Act. The board declares that no share shall be issued for less than par value and that the subscribed capital is not held in escrow or subject to any unlawful anti-dilution commitment. 2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the establishment of a corporate banking relationship with [Bank Name] and the opening of all demand, deposit, foreign currency, and letter-of-credit accounts. The Chairperson, the General Manager, and [Accountant] are designated as the authorized signatories, and any two of such signatories shall be required to execute each payment instrument, loan agreement, or guarantee. The bank is instructed to honor only resolutions-approved corporate purposes and to provide all statements and tax reporting data to the statutory auditor. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be situated at [Full Address, Taiwan jurisdiction]. The General Manager is authorized to execute the office lease, register the office with the Company and Commercial Registration Authority, post the company name plate, and maintain the statutory records and seal at such address. Any relocation of the registered office shall require a further board resolution. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following persons are elected and appointed: [Name] as Director and Chairperson; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Supervisor; and [Name] as General Manager and Chief Compliance Officer. The officers so appointed are authorized to execute all incorporation, tax, labor, licensing, and operating documents, to affix the company seal, to make representations before the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Financial Supervisory Commission, and to delegate ancillary powers as required. 5. General Resolutions. The officers are instructed to apply for foreign investment registration, company registration, tax registration, and the insurance surveyor license. The board ratifies all lawful acts previously performed on behalf of the Company and directs that these resolutions be filed with the minutes and be binding upon all successors and transferees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Company Name and Business Scope Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval One-Stop Online System, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must first access the MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Online System and file an application for reservation of the company name and business scope. The application must list the proposed English name, a transliterated Chinese name if used internally, and a business scope clause covering vessel hull and cargo damage inspection, marine claims surveying, loss adjustment, and related maritime support services under ISIC 5222. The system automatically screens for identical or confusingly similar names and consults the Financial Supervisory Commission on regulated keywords such as insurance and surveyor. Because the business will be a regulated insurance surveying company, the pre-approved business scope must not omit the regulated term. If the name includes a restricted word, the FSC comment must be attached. The applicant should secure signature notarization by a Taiwan notary public or an overseas Taiwan representative office if the foreign investor signs abroad. The approval is valid for six months and may be extended once for an additional six months.
required_dossiers: Completed company name and business scope pre-approval application form
Certificate of incorporation or business registration of the foreign investor
Passport copies of the authorized representative and ultimate beneficial owner
Power of attorney executed by the foreign investor
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Business plan describing marine cargo and hull claims survey services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is queried, respond online within fourteen days, submit a disclaimer letter for restricted words, or file three alternative names. If the business scope is suspended due to regulatory ambiguity, amend the phrase to state marine insurance claims surveying and loss adjustment only and resubmit with a legal opinion if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) and designated foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form A Foreign Investment Application to the Investment Commission, MOEA, together with corporate existence documents of the ultimate beneficial owner, audited financial statements, the draft Articles of Incorporation, the business plan, and the name reservation certificate. The Investment Commission may request a confidentiality undertaking if the surveyor will access cargo manifests or insured vessel data. After the Foreign Investment Approval is issued, the investor must open a bank account in the company name and remit the subscribed capital from an overseas account. The designated bank will prepare a Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate and report to the Central Bank; the funds must be credited before the CPA issues the capital verification report. The investor must maintain the source-of-funds evidence and the approval letter for at least five years. If investment involves intangible assets or equipment contributed in kind, a valuation report approved by the Investment Commission is required.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form A
Foreign investor corporate existence certificate and board resolution authorizing the investment
Audited financial statements or bank reference letter of the investor
Power of attorney and passport copies
Name and business scope reservation certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation and business plan
Capital remittance cable advice and Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission suspends the application, supply missing notarized documents within thirty days or apply for an amendment. If the capital source is questioned, provide bank reference letters, audited financial statements, and a fund source declaration. If the proposed investment amount is considered inadequate for the licensed activity, revise the capital amount and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration and First Board Meeting Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Service, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After capital is received, the directors must convene the first board meeting and adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, authorize the issuance of shares, approve the registered office, appoint officers, and adopt the company seal. The certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report based on the bank statement. The incorporation registration application must be filed through the Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Service or at the Department of Commerce within fifteen days after the meeting. The filing must include a completed registration application, original Articles of Incorporation, board meeting minutes, CPA capital verification report, lease or consent documents for the registered office, and identification documents for directors, supervisor, and manager. The registrar examines statutory compliance and, if satisfactory, issues the Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Number. The company must then apply for taxation registration before commencing any business activity.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Incorporation Registration
Original Articles of Incorporation signed by all subscribers
First Board Meeting Minutes and Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
CPA Capital Verification Report
Registered office lease, consent, and evidence of lawful use
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Identity documents of directors, supervisor, and general manager
Company seal registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Commerce issues a correction notice, respond within fifteen days. If the capital verification report is defective, engage the certifying CPA to amend and resubmit. If the registered office consent is defective, replace the lease or obtain a new landlord consent and re-file the registration application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, and Premises Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; local Municipal Labor Affairs Department; local Fire Department and Building Public Safety Inspection Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days after company registration, the company must obtain a Tax Registration Certificate from the National Taxation Bureau, apply for the Uniform Invoice Commissioner, register for business tax, and register as a withholding tax payer. Simultaneously, the company must complete labor insurance, health insurance, labor pension, and employment qualification filings for all employees under the Labor Insurance Act and Labor Standards Act. For the office premises, the company must file building public safety inspection and fire safety inspection certificates with the local municipal fire department. If the company will operate any warehouse, workshop, or laboratory at the survey site, it must also file the relevant building use, structural safety, occupational safety, and environmental registration documents. The National Taxation Bureau will assign a tax identification number and issue the Certificate of Tax Registration. The local labor department will issue a workplace safety inspection clearance where required for maritime support operations.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Tax Registration Application Form
Uniform Invoice Application Form
Lease or ownership document for registered office
Building Public Safety Inspection Certificate
Fire Safety Equipment Self-Inspection Form
Labor and health insurance registration forms
Work rules and employee roster
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries the revenue classification, submit an explanation of the marine surveying fee structure and VAT treatment. If the fire safety inspection fails, complete remedial works and request re-inspection within ten days. If the labor department identifies workplace safety deficiencies, submit a corrective action plan and obtain re-certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sector-Specific Insurance Surveyor License and Operational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Insurance Bureau, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); Taiwan International Ports Corporation for port access; local Fire Department and Occupational Safety Authority for physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing marine insurance surveying operations, the company must obtain the Insurance Surveyor Company License from the Insurance Bureau of the Financial Supervisory Commission. The application shall include the company registration certificate, evidence that each individual surveyor satisfies the qualification requirements of the Insurance Surveyor Qualification and Registration Regulations, an office fire safety certificate, professional indemnity insurance certificate, and a statement of internal control procedures for handling underwriter assignments. If survey activities involve boarding vessels or entering terminals, the company must coordinate with port authority security and obtain terminal access clearance in accordance with International Ship and Port Facility Security requirements. Because no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing process is carried out, an Environmental Impact Assessment is not mandated; however, if a small laboratory is later established for cargo contamination testing, the company shall file an Environmental Registration with the Environmental Protection Administration before installing any equipment. The FSC license must be renewed or validated annually, and changes in qualified surveyors must be reported within fifteen days.
required_dossiers: FSC Insurance Surveyor Company License Application Form
Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Number Certificate
Individual insurance surveyor qualification certificates
Fire Safety and Building Public Safety Inspection Certificates
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Statement of internal control procedures
Port terminal access clearance if vessel boarding is planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC requests additional evidence, submit the required documents within thirty days. If individual surveyor qualifications are insufficient, hire an additional licensed surveyor or arrange a transfer of registration. If a port access application is denied, revise the security plan and resubmit. If an EPA environmental registration is triggered by an ancillary laboratory, submit the registration package within thirty days and do not operate the laboratory until clearance is granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Insurance Bureau, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); Taiwan International Ports Corporation for port access; local municipal Fire Department, Building Public Safety Inspection Authority, and Occupational Safety and Health Authority for workplace and premises clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Insurance Surveyor Company License for Marine Cargo and Hull Claims Surveying and Loss Adjustment under the Insurance Law and the Regulations Governing Insurance Surveyors.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan jurisdiction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable for pure marine insurance surveying and office-based operations. If an ancillary cargo-testing laboratory, survey workshop, or storage facility is established, the operation will require at least an Environmental Registration, and depending on scale and hazard potential, a Category B environmental impact assessment report may be required before construction or installation of equipment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any ancillary laboratory or workshop: process wastewater must comply with the Effluent Standards under the Water Pollution Control Act, with chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 100 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, and pH between 6 and 9. Fugitive volatile organic compound emissions must remain below 0.6 kg/hr; if above this threshold, an air pollution permit and annual compliance report are required. Hazardous waste generated from oil-contaminated cargo samples, marine diesel residues, or used sample solvents must be stored in approved containers, manifested on the EPA hazardous waste tracking system, and transported by a licensed hazardous waste carrier to a permitted treatment facility within ninety days of generation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire Services Act is required for the registered office and any survey staging area; this includes a building public safety inspection certificate, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, evacuation route signage, an evacuation plan, and fire drill records. Civil Defense clearance involves verifying that the premises comply with the public safety inspection standards and that responsible personnel are trained in emergency response. Occupational clearance requires a workplace risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including personal protective equipment for surveyors, safe work procedures for vessel access, cargo hatch inspection, and confined-space entry, plus accident reporting to the labor authority within eight hours of any serious workplace incident. If the company does not conduct manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing, no industrial plant license is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration, enforced through the regional National Taxation Bureaus (Taipei, Northern, Central, Southern, Kaohsiung). The statutory online electronic portal is the Ministry of Finance e-Tax Service Portal at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw, together with the Ministry of Finance Business Tax e-Declaration System for periodic VAT filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) Limited Company in Taiwan must first secure foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. After the company is registered with Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs, the entity automatically receives an eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBIN), which serves as the universal national tax identification number for corporate income tax, value-added business tax, and customs declarations. Before commencing business, or within 30 days after company registration if business has commenced, the WFOE must file a Business Entity Tax Registration Application with the National Taxation Bureau in whose jurisdiction the registered address or fixed place of business is located. The submission bundle must include the company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, foreign investor and shareholder documentation, board and resident manager appointment evidence, lease agreement or proof of business premise, and a letter of authorization for local fiscal agents. The tax office enters the UBIN into the tax database and activates the business tax account. If the foreign entity has no fixed place of business in Taiwan but performs taxable marine survey services inside Taiwan, it must appoint a fiscal representative and apply for registration through the same regional National Taxation Bureau before supplying any Taiwan-sourced services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election, and there is no general hybrid-mismatch elective mechanism under the Income Tax Act or the Business Tax Act. A Taiwan-incorporated WFOE limited company is automatically classified as a resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income, and it is mandatorily registered as a value-added taxpayer for business tax purposes. No pass-through classification or consolidated tax filing election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax under the Business Tax Act (also known as Taiwan VAT or the Uniform Invoice business tax system)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold applies for mandatory business tax registration; every business entity with a fixed place of business or engaging in taxable activities in Taiwan must register before commencement. Small-scale enterprises whose average monthly taxable sales do not exceed New Taiwan Dollars 200,000 may elect the simplified special business tax regime at a lower effective rate instead of the standard VAT computation, but any WFOE providing marine insurance survey services to commercial underwriters is ordinarily treated as a full VAT business entity required to issue Uniform Invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the Uniform Invoice system for all VAT-registered business entities. The WFOE must procure serially numbered Uniform Invoices from the National Taxation Bureau and issue a Uniform Invoice for every taxable sale of goods or services. For business-to-business and business-to-consumer sales where electronic Uniform Invoices are used, the taxpayer must adopt the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice platform and transmit XML invoice data through the statutory Government Turnkey Server or certified API channel, generally without extension, within the filing cycle. The e-Invoice platform applies QR-code security features, a unique invoice number, and central data storage for anti-fraud cross-checking. Hard-copy Uniform Invoices do not require a separate digital stamp at issuance, but the registered invoice series must be reconciled with all issued, voided, and unused invoices in the VAT periodic filing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of Taiwan's Business Tax Act, a zero percent VAT rate applies to goods that are actually exported outside Taiwan, and to services supplied to a foreign enterprise, foreign individual, or foreign institution where the service is used or consumed outside Taiwan. For the marine insurance survey business covering vessel hull and cargo damage claims, zero-rating is eligible when the survey report, damage assessment, inspection certificate, and claim-adjustment deliverable are provided to a foreign marine underwriter or overseas policyholder and the economic benefit is realized outside Taiwan. The service must be genuinely exported rather than consumed in Taiwan; inspection or surveying performed on a vessel or cargo within Taiwan operational waters for a domestic insurer's Taiwan claims file remains subject to the standard 5% rate. Qualifying offshore digital services are also zero-rated if electronically supplied and used outside Taiwan, but the core services in this business remain physical marine survey activities that must meet the export-of-services documentation test.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) for goods supplied directly in connection with an export transaction
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill issued by the carrier evidencing movement of goods from Taiwan to a foreign destination
Full executed marine survey and claims inspection contract specifying the foreign underwriter or overseas insured party and the Taiwan exporter or service provider
Commercial invoice and tax Uniform Invoice (where applicable) addressed to the foreign counterparty

Foreign Exchange Settlement Receipt or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank evidencing receipt of foreign-currency settlement for the zero-rated export service
Complete marine survey report, photographic evidence, damage assessment certificate, and photocopies of vessel or cargo documents demonstrating the deliverable was used by the foreign beneficiary
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau applies strict audit scrutiny to zero-rated export services by comparing the export declaration, bill of lading, survey contract, commercial invoice, foreign-currency payment evidence, and banking remittance records. The taxpayer must retain the full export documentation bundle for at least five years from the filing date, and foreign-currency proceeds should be repatriated and evidenced within the 180-day statutory substantiation window. If the taxpayer claims zero-rating without genuine export documentation, or if the documentation is found to be fraudulent, forged, or commercially implausible, the tax authority will assess the underpaid business tax at 5%, impose additional interest from the original due date, and apply under the Business Tax Act a penalty of one to five times the amount of the tax evaded. Where deliberate fraudulent invoices or forged customs documents are used, the responsible person may be subject to criminal liability, imprisonment, and further fines under the Taiwan Tax Evasion and Criminal Law framework, and the tax authority may order the suspension of the taxpayer's Uniform Invoice purchasing privilege until compliance is restored.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime. RMB is freely convertible for most current account transactions, but the capital account remains highly regulated. A WFOE must obtain SAFE registration and open a designated FDI capital account; capital received from the Taiwan-based parent can only be converted with an underlying negative-list check and funds must be used for the declared business purpose. Profit remittance to shareholders requires audited financial statements, board resolution, enterprise income tax return and tax payment proof; the bank will scrutinize whether the WFOE has completed annual industrial and commercial filing and foreign investment information reporting. Service trade income from marine surveying is a current account credit and enjoys relatively free convertibility, provided the contract, invoice and survey deliverables are authentic. However, any remittance to tax havens or payments not matching the service description will be blocked under SAFE truthfulness and compliance review. Cross-border foreign debt, equity transfers, liquidation proceeds and any form of offshore borrowing require separate quota or registration. In practice, converting dividends or returning capital to the Taiwan parent is the most difficult liquidity action and must be supported by a full documentary chain and tax settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exported goods, the exporter must normally bring the foreign-currency proceeds back to a domestic designated account within the agreed trade credit period and no later than 120 days after export customs declaration unless approved under a different collection method; if the proceeds are not received, the WFOE must report to SAFE's Goods Trade Monitoring System. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio under the current SAFE framework; the exporter may retain 100% of the foreign currency in a current-account settlement account and convert to RMB voluntarily. For marine insurance survey services exported under trade-in-services, there is no surrender requirement, but the receipt must be declared on the Service Trade International Revenue and Expenditure Declaration Form and must be matched with the survey contract and delivery evidence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI and RMB Basic Operational Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to open domestic deposit accounts, RMB clearing records, FDI capital-account collection services or statutory capital verification reports for an onshore mainland China WFOE. They are legally barred from serving as the primary treasury rail for this entity. An EMI can be used only as a secondary gate for incidental overseas supplier payments if routed through a licensed partner bank, but it cannot replace a tier-one domestic commercial bank for SAFE filing, foreign exchange conversion, tax withholding, or capital account compliance. WFOE treasury operations must maintain their core clearing accounts with an onshore bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch attendance is mandatory for the opening of the RMB Basic Deposit Account and the FDI foreign exchange capital account. The statutory legal representative or a board-authorized officer holding a notarized power of attorney must appear in the branch for the PBOC-required customer due diligence interview. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial corporate KYC interview; the bank may permit a video interview for supplemental verification but the original corporate approval, identification documents and company chops must still be presented at the branch before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a Taiwan-based intermediate holding chain and nominee shareholder structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpts for all entities in the ownership chain; shareholder register and UBO declaration signed by each natural-person owner; passports and tax identification numbers of the ultimate beneficial owners; certificate of incorporation of the Taiwan parent; board register and directors' identity documents; notarized confirmation that no undisclosed nominee shareholders or trusts sit above the WFOE; audited financial statements of the holding entity for the last three years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine insurance survey income paid by overseas underwriters and reinsurers appears inconsistent with the underlying claims and loss-adjustment files.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed marine survey contracts; detailed survey reports with date, location and inspection photographs; underwriter instruction letters; insurer loss-advice documents; claim settlement ledger; correspondence with loss adjusters; itemized invoices matched to each survey job; GPS or vessel-log evidence; vessel/cargo policy references; payment receipts and international service trade declaration forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid transfer of funds between the FDI capital account and the operating current account followed by immediate third-party disbursements, suggesting possible round-tripping or misuse of capital account funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and twelve-month cash flow budget; source-of-funds evidence from the Taiwan parent; capital contribution schedule; certified capital verification report issued by a Chinese certified public accountant; office lease, payroll records, survey equipment purchase invoices and calibration contracts; monthly bank statements with transaction narratives; internal treasury authorization policy and conversion approval records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment counterparty is subject to sanctions, PEP screening, or is located in a high-risk jurisdiction in the reinsurance and marine insurance chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions/PEP screening reports for every beneficiary and payee; full corporate register and beneficial ownership of all insurers and reinsurers; regulatory licences of counterparty insurers; jurisdiction risk assessment report; enhanced due diligence questionnaire and adverse media search results; indemnity or warranty clauses from the counterparty; source of funds evidence from the claim settlement; trade-specific policy contracts and loss reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must remit the equity injection via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered FDI foreign exchange capital account at a designated domestic tier-one bank. The remittance references must include the SAFE FDI registration code and the bank-designated FX purpose code for foreign-invested enterprise equity injection. After receipt, the bank reports the cross-border receipt to SAFE and the WFOE's certified public accountant performs statutory capital verification. Only after the capital verification report is issued can the funds be settled into RMB and transferred to the operational RMB account for approved expenses. Wise and other EMI rails are not acceptable for FDI capital injection or statutory capital verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For marine surveying operational payments, SWIFT MT103 is the primary rail for direct wire disbursements to overseas subcontractors, professional indemnity insurers and equipment suppliers. For large procurement of specialized survey equipment, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the domestic bank is the appropriate rail, supported by invoice, transport document and quality certificate. For contested claim settlements, documentary collections may be used with condition documents such as survey reports and independent adjuster certificates. All outbound disbursements require underlying contract, invoice, tax clearance and the Service Trade International Revenue and Expenditure Declaration Form; a standalone Wise transfer cannot satisfy SAFE reporting and tax dossier requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD deliverable forward contracts executed with a domestic commercial bank, supported by genuine current account exposures such as marine survey service fees receivable and operational payables.
FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps with a domestic bank, limited to existing SAFE-registered foreign debt or long-term trade exposure.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards in CNH may be used by the Taiwan parent or offshore affiliates, but the onshore WFOE may not enter speculative NDF positions; onshore hedging must be delivered and bank-approved.
FX options are permissible only when approved by the bank's treasury risk committee and matched with confirmed marine insurance claim settlement inflows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting to approve the directors' business report, audited financial statements (if threshold-triggered), and profit appropriation or loss coverage resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting in accordance with Taiwan Company Act; no filing to the government—the approved minutes must be kept in the statutory minute book and made available to MOEA on inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each fiscal year; calendar-year WFOE must hold the meeting by 30 June of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA may impose an administrative fine on responsible directors of NT$20,000–NT$100,000 (about USD 650–3,250) and, in persistent default, apply to the court for compulsory dissolution/strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement filing with the company registration authority, including the balance sheet, statement of comprehensive income, cash flow statement, and statement of changes in equity; CPA-audited version required when thresholds apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) — Company Registration Office via the local Northern/Central/Southern Regional Commercial Registration Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year company by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are subject to the same administrative fines as a convention default; repeated refusal to file permits MOEA to revoke the company's registration, leading to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification and update of the Shareholders' Register, Directors' Register, and statutory minute book, including recording of all share ownership movements and changes in beneficial ownership during the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: On-site statutory corporate records; inspected by MOEA and tax authorities upon request; no separate annual booklet filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updates are required within 15 days after each transfer or appointment change; annual internal confirmation shall be completed on or before the annual shareholders' meeting (30 June for calendar-year WFOEs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unrecorded transfers are ineffective against the company; inaccurate registers expose directors to civil liability and administrative fines if MOEA inspection or court proceeding identifies hidden shareholders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory CPA audit applies where paid-in capital is at least NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000) or annual operating revenue is at least NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3,200,000); the MOEA may also require an audit where financial structure conditions indicate necessity; a license-regulated marine insurance surveyor should additionally comply with the FSC's audit/examination requirements for registered insurance auxiliary enterprises
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must follow Taiwan IFRS as recognized by the Financial Supervisory Commission for public companies; private WFOEs may consistently apply Taiwan IFRS or ROC GAAP. Accounts are kept in New Taiwan Dollars and must conform to the Business Entity Accounting Act and the Company Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not operate a separate annual UBO filing to a beneficial-ownership register for a non-public WFOE. The company maintains a Register of Members in which every share transfer and ultimate owner/member is recognized; transfer is effective against the company only after entry in the register. The board must review and confirm the register at each annual shareholders' meeting; material shareholding or ultimate-beneficiary changes during the year must be recorded promptly and disclosed for annual confirmation to the shareholders.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,500 per annum for a registered agent / registered office / annual company secretarial service in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 per annum for a certified financial statement audit of a small-to-mid-size marine insurance surveyor WFOE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-owned enterprises are effectively taxed at 20% on taxable income. Preferential deductions include a 20% investment tax credit for qualified R&D expenditures under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, and certain shipping-related income may be exempt if the enterprise holds a vessel registry license. Retained earnings are subject to an additional 5% undistributed surplus tax unless distributed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 109-1) electronically filed via the National Taxation Bureau eTax Portal (網路報稅及上傳)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year filers, the deadline is May 31. Extension of one month may be granted by the National Taxation Bureau for consolidated returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenues: insurance survey fees, marine claims inspection services, and miscellaneous income from vessel damage assessments. Recoveries from reinsurers are included unless held in trust.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident enterprises without a permanent establishment in Taiwan must report only Taiwan-source revenue. If books are incomplete, the tax authority may assess a deemed profit rate of 15% on gross service income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of operations: direct labour for surveyors, cost of vessel and equipment hire, fuel, insurance, and subcontractor payments attributable to the survey services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign costs are deductible only if fully documented and if an arm's-length allocation is demonstrated. A non-resident filer must submit an audited cost statement certified by a Taiwan CPA if claiming deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: employee salaries, office rents, liability insurance, professional memberships, and travel expenses for on-site vessel survey.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred outside Taiwan must be allocated based on a formula filed in advance with the National Taxation Bureau. The bureau may re-allocate expenditures under the general anti-avoidance rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before credits: computed as operating income minus costs, expenses, and losses, adjusted by non-taxable income and disallowed expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident enterprises generally report taxable income equal to gross Taiwan-source revenue × deemed profit rate (15% for marine survey services) minus income tax credits, unless they opt to maintain full books and file a complete return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retained earnings tax (5% on undistributed surplus) – applies to earnings for which no dividend distribution is made in the following calendar year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign corporate shareholder may request a remission of the retained earnings tax if it executes a dividend distribution declaration within the statutory reinvestment timeline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a bona fide extension results in a surcharge of 1% per month of unpaid tax (maximum 10%), and an additional penalty of 2% for every two-month period (maximum 20%) if the return remains unfiled. Failure to file a return when tax due exceeds NT$120,000 is subject to up to 5 years imprisonment for the responsible person.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 21% for non-resident individuals. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (where applied), the rate may be reduced to 10% for a parent owning at least 25% for a 12-month period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty or cross-strait relief, a non-resident beneficiary must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction's fiscal authority; (2) provide the TRC, a Declaration of Beneficial Ownership, and the original certificate of residence to the Taiwan withholding agent; (3) the withholding agent files Form 102 with the National Taxation Bureau before the dividend distribution date; (4) after approval, the reduced rate is applied to the distribution and a check for the excess withholding is issued. Processing takes 2–4 weeks. The Taiwan tax authority must be granted access to verify the beneficial owner's substantive business activities in the home jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate of 20%; interest (arm's length) statutory rate of 15%. Under an applicable tax agreement, royalty and interest rates may be reduced to 10% (and interest to 0%, if paid to a financial institution under some treaties). Payments to entities resident in tax-haven jurisdictions are generally not entitled to treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be prepared if the aggregate of all related-party transactions (including marine survey service fees, reinsurance premium sharing, and claims commissions) exceeds NT$200 million in a given year. A Master File is mandatory for multinational groups with annual consolidated revenue exceeding NT$2 billion. The Country-by-Country Report is required when group annual consolidated revenue exceeds NT$27 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has not enacted a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute applicable to all entities. Instead, the Income Tax Act, the Company Act, and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) impose a 'real substance' requirement in practice. The tax authority disregards a letterbox company that lacks a physical office, employee payroll, bank account, and substantive decision-making in Taiwan. The doctrine is applied both in the transfer pricing context (denial of treaty benefits for no business purpose) and in corporate registration (where the tax authority may re-attribute the income to the foreign parent).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating survey fee income, overstating deductible costs, fabricating loss reserves for marine claims, or using shell sub-contractors to shift profit offshore without a taxable nexus.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of up to 3 times the underpaid tax amount and a daily surcharge of 0.05% for delayed payment. Deliberate non-filing with tax due over NT$120,000 carries imprisonment for a maximum of 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign falsified returns or order concealed offshore transactions are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and interest. The Taiwan tax authority may impose a travel ban (控制出境) and invoke criminal liability against the 'responsible person' (代表人), resulting in imprisonment. Corporate veil lifting under Company Act Article 139 applies when the entity is used to mask fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Taiwan WFOE with a nominee director, no office, no staff, and no local service activity; interposing the entity solely to convert service fees into tax-favoured repatriation under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority re-characterizes the entity as a transparent conduit, disallows all intercompany expenses, and imposes a 5% surcharge on the re-determined taxable income plus monthly interest. In egregious cases the registration itself is revoked by the Commercial Ministry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the actual beneficial owner may be held personally liable for the unpaid tax through the application of the 'piercing the corporate veil' doctrine, and may be disqualified from acting as a director in Taiwan for up to 3 years. If the shell structure is used to conceal AML risks, criminal imprisonment up to 2 years applies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting premium payments or claim settlements in cash or through unregulated payment rails without obtaining beneficial ownership declarations, or conducting survey work for sanctioned vessels or insurance companies without enhanced due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, fines of NT$500,000 to NT$5,000,000 and suspension of the company's business licence for repeat or serious violations; failure to maintain transaction records results in a fine of up to NT$1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to imprisonment for up to 2 years and a fine of up to NT$5,000,000 if they intentionally or through gross negligence fail to implement an AML program. The corporate veil is pierced where officers funnelled proceeds to a foreign parent; the court may attach personal bank accounts and impose a 5-year travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting marine survey service fees between the Taiwan WFOE and its overseas parent or sister company without a documented CUP; undercharging for claims inspection services to shift profit to a tax haven; failing to file related-party disclosure schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority makes a primary adjustment, increases taxable income to reflect an arm's-length price, and applies a 5% surcharge on the underpaid tax (maximum 30% of the deficiency). A secondary adjustment may deem a 20% withholding tax on constructive dividends if the correction is not remitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement non-arm's-length fees may be sued by the company for breach of fiduciary duties, and the tax authority may issue a deficiency assessment against the controlling foreign shareholder as a secondary taxpayer. In aggravated cases, a criminal referral for tax fraud is made under Article 110.
